svg.title: From a public Sketchfab model to a usable 3D file
svg.desc: From a public Sketchfab model to a usable 3D file: dag diagram, 6 nodes, 7 edges. Flow: Read public viewer → Decode mesh; Read public viewer → Descramble textures; Read public viewer → Build glTF (Materials + scene); Decode mesh → Build glTF; Descramble textures → Build glTF; Build glTF → GLB file; …. Full data in hw:payload.

rdf:Description.dc:title: From a public Sketchfab model to a usable 3D file
rdf:Description.dc:creator: HyperWeave Compositor v0.4.7 (InnerAura Labs)

hw:zone.reason: var() does not resolve in an SVG presentation attribute, so this paint is decided at compose time

hw:reasoning.hw:intent: One topology graph carrying BOTH faces: white cards on the light base scope, the dark plate behind prefers-color-scheme. The same file drops into a light README and a dark one and reads as drawn for each, rather than as a light diagram someone dimmed.
hw:reasoning.hw:approach: Geometry is solved once and is substrate-blind — the 64px fan pitch, the 92px convergence pitch, the 178px flywheel arcs, every card box through the one sizing seam — so only paint forks. The genome layer rescopes from `svg, :root` to the artifact's own #uid, and the dark face restates the same roles inside the media query: card fill moves to a 3-stop eased ramp (crown, chassis-offset mid, long tail to the floor) with an edge-stroke gradient down its own ladder, and each flow slot gets its own --dna-flow-{i} so both faces resolve independently.
hw:reasoning.hw:tradeoffs: Elevation's geometry cannot follow the palette — var() does not resolve in the filter's geometry attributes (dx/dy/stdDeviation are attribute-only) — while its paint can: flood-color and flood-opacity accept var(). The light face's two-layer lift (0/1/2 at 5 percent over 0/9/20 at 5.5) and the dark face's 0/6/12 seat keep literal geometry selected by paired CSS rules, so retuning either is a config edit. The seat is also ground-keyed — it casts ink outside the card, so it only draws on a plate the artifact owns; on a bare ground the lift pair carries elevation instead, trading depth for not banding an unknown host.
